concerns.text: FR-006 requires a paired t-test of "policy acceptance rates AND final scores", but T009's t-test consumes only reasoning scores; acceptance_rate_proxy/acceptance_rate_sync are recorded but never statistically compared. Half of FR-006 is silently dropped.

No task produces the consolidated metrics artifact conforming to metrics.schema.yaml (correlation_results per level, statistical_tests with bonferroni_corrected_p, latency_reduction, collinearity_check in one object). Metrics are scattered across test_metrics.json, t_test_results.json, latency_metrics.json, final_consistency_summary.json with different field names — the metrics contract is orphaned and Constitution IV traceability to a single metrics.json is weakened.

T003 silently narrows the spec's Llama-3-8B reference to Llama-3.2-1B/3B "per the compute budget". The spec's RAM-feasibility assumption is written around the 8B model; this is a retroactive requirement narrowing recorded only in a run log, not sanctioned by a spec-level decision. Either amend the spec assumption explicitly or justify the scaling in the spec.

SC-005 mandates maintaining n ≥ 300 total samples when reducing dataset size for the 6-hour budget. T004's early-stop rule ("stop early only if >300 samples done") and the ≥100-per-level verification do not enforce or check the n ≥ 300 floor; the constraint can be violated without any gate failing.

FR-002 and the spec mandate FP8 via llama.cpp on CPU, but FP8 GGUF is not a standard llama.cpp quantization; the plan lists onnxruntime as fallback yet no task defines when/how the fallback engine is selected. T004's per-level coverage gate ("fail loudly if any level has zero successful samples") has no recovery path, risking an unavoidable hard failure of a spec-mandated level.

Plan T019 and the data model specify PCA-reduced features (["PCA1","PCA2"]) for the predictor; T006 trains KRR on raw gradient_norm/local_curvature with no PCA step. Either restore the PCA step or update plan/data-model to document the change — as written the task contradicts the documented feature pipeline.

Plan enumerates T015–T032 while tasks.md uses T001–T013 with a different decomposition and no mapping. Scientific content is largely covered, but plan↔task ID traceability is broken; add a traceability note mapping old plan IDs to new task IDs.
